subject: Retry amplification causing sustained tail errors — status notice & postmortem plan
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@kitehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in 5xx & partial responses from /v1/generate

Hi Sergio,

We started seeing a sustained spike in 5xx errors and a band of partial responses from the hosted API (us-west region) around 08:45 PDT this morning. Our ingest pipeline logs a lot of client retries; overall latency P95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s. Affected endpoints are /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream.

Examples: 1) request id 9b2f... returned 504 after server-side retries; 2) session 7c1a... returned truncated JSON (missing final tokens). Our customer experience team is receiving increased complaint tickets.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing retry amplification or queuing backpressure? Any ETA for mitigation or a status page link we can share with our customers?

Thanks,
Elaine
Ops
KiteHealth

--
Elaine Park
Site Reliability Lead, KiteHealth
ops@kitehealth.com

Subject: Re: sudden increase in 5xx & partial responses from /v1/generate

Thanks Elaine — I see the spike, and we’re actively triaging. I’ll keep you updated but wanted to confirm a couple quick things:

- Are you still seeing retries from your SDKs or from your edge? If possible, can you share a short window (10-15 minutes) of request IDs?
- Are these customer-facing production keys (i.e., hitting shared hosted pool) or a dedicated pool?

Interim steps we’re moving on immediately:
- Activating an emergency route to a lower-utilization pool for your account to reduce queuing pressure.
- Enabling additional logging of retry chains so we can see amplification loops.
- Publishing a brief status notice to our status page (draft below) so you can point customers to official comms.

Draft status blurb (we will publish within 30 min unless you object):
"We are investigating elevated error rates and partial responses affecting generation and streaming endpoints in the US-West region. Customers may observe higher tail latency and intermittent 5xx/partial payloads. Our engineers are mitigating routing and queuing pressure and will provide updates here."

I’m looping Hannah and Marissa for support/ops coordination and Rishi for SRE. Expect a targeted mitigation in the next 20–30 minutes.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: sudden increase in 5xx & partial responses from /v1/generate

Forwarding Elaine’s report — I’ve validated the US-West telemetry and confirmed a sustained increase in queued request depth across the shared hosting pool. Early signal indicates retry-amplification: client SDK timers are triggering retries while requests are already being requeued internally, causing cascading duplicates and head-of-line blocking.

Planned immediate ops actions:
- Apply per-account rate smoothing for KiteHealth (will limit short-burst retry fanout).
- Offload KiteHealth traffic to warm standby pool with relaxed batching for 15 mins.
- Throttle internal retry-forwarding logic where duplicate signature detected (hotfix).

I’ve drafted the status notice below and attached a copy of the proposed text (status-draft.txt). Please review quickly — we need to push to the public status page and to customers.

Draft status page entry (proposed):
Title: Elevated tail errors and partial responses — US-West
Status: Identified / Investigating
Impact: Customers may see intermittent 5xx and truncated generation payloads from hosted endpoints.
Cause (investigating): Increased client retry amplification plus internal requeueing leading to queue saturation.
Mitigation: Offloading impacted accounts to standby pool; applying short-term request smoothing and duplicate suppression.
ETA for next update: 30 minutes

---

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: retry amplification incident (US-West) — mitigation and next steps

Hi Elaine and KiteHealth team,

Thanks for your patience while we mitigated the incident. Summary and next steps below.

What happened (tl;dr):
Between ~08:45–10:10 PDT on 2028-06-01, our hosted generation pool in US-West experienced queue saturation caused by retry amplification. Client SDK retry timers combined with internal requeueing created duplicate request amplification leading to head-of-line blocking and partial/truncated responses.

What we did:
- Immediately offloaded impacted customers (including KiteHealth) to a warm standby pool to reduce queue depth.
- Implemented per-account short-term rate smoothing to dampen retry fanout.
- Deployed a duplicate-request suppression hotfix to avoid reprocessing identical request fingerprints.
- Published a status update while mitigation was in progress: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2028-06-retry-amplification

Impact:
- Customers in US-West may have seen elevated 5xx rates, truncated payloads, and higher tail latency for ~1.5 hours.
- We estimate ~0.2% of requests during the window were affected end-to-end.

Permanent follow-ups we’ll take:
- Expand duplicate suppression to cross-pool routing logic.
- Improve SDK guidance and backoff defaults to reduce out-of-the-box amplification.
- Add a circuit-breaker for excessive requeue depth with automatic routing to standby pools (SRE project).
- Deliver a public postmortem document (target: 2028-06-05).

Attachments: postmortem-2028-06-retry-amplification.pdf (interim draft) — includes timeline and proposed remediation roadmap.

If you’d like a synchronous debrief, I’m available tomorrow morning; otherwise we’ll share the full postmortem link once finalized: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ABC-postmortem

Apologies for the disruption — we took steps to reduce recurrence and will follow up with code and SDK changes.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
